headline: Broad Rally Carries Wednesday Higher, Though Software Bears the Brunt
body_html:
Equities closed in the green on Wednesday, September 2, as buyers held the upper hand across most of the session. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a comfortable 346-to-198 margin within the Jaleel Capital universe of 548 names, underscoring the rally's genuine breadth rather than an index-level illusion driven by a handful of heavyweights.

The clearest sector narrative was a rotation toward tangible-asset and defensive names and away from high-multiple software. Materials led all groups with a gain of 1.17%, followed closely by Healthcare at 1.11% and Semiconductors at 0.91%. Energy and Consumer also finished solidly positive. Industrials eked out a 0.30% advance, while Software was the lone sector in the red, shedding 0.88% as earnings-driven selling cascaded through database, observability, and customer-experience names.

Geopolitical unease over renewed U.S.-Iran hostilities and tightening Strait of Hormuz shipping lanes provided a quiet tailwind for Materials and Energy — a dynamic worth watching as military activity shows little sign of abating before November. With bond yields overseas pressing multi-decade highs, Wednesday's domestic resilience looks all the more notable.

briefs.headline: Sarepta Surges to Session's Top Spot on Biotech Momentum
briefs.body: Sarepta Therapeutics vaulted 8.81% Wednesday, making it the session's single largest percentage gainer. The move propelled Healthcare-Biotech to the forefront of the day's winners and helped lift the broader Healthcare sector. Alnylam added 8.65%, reinforcing the impression of genuine, broad-based buying interest in biotech.

briefs.headline: Connectivity Chipmaker Credo Craters More Than 20%
briefs.body: Credo Technology shed more than a fifth of its value in Wednesday's session, the steepest single-day drop in the Jaleel Capital universe. The selloff rippled through connectivity semiconductor names and served as a stark counterpoint to the otherwise constructive tape. No other name in the universe came close to matching that magnitude of decline.

briefs.headline: Software Sector Drags as MongoDB, Palo Alto Hit Hard
briefs.body: MongoDB plunged 13.54% and Palo Alto Networks fell 9.28%, anchoring a punishing session for software-adjacent names. Datadog dropped 6.53% and Sprinklr lost 8.55%, painting a consistent picture of institutional selling across the group. The sector's 0.88% loss stood as Wednesday's only red column on the sector leaderboard.

briefs.headline: Iran Tensions Tighten Grip on Hormuz Shipping Lanes
briefs.body: Reports that Iran has blacklisted additional vessels attempting passage through the Strait of Hormuz injected fresh uncertainty into energy markets Wednesday. Combined with signals from Washington that military strikes could intensify past November, traders appear to be pricing a sustained risk premium into commodity-linked equities, with Energy finishing up 0.89% on the session.

briefs.headline: Materials and Steel Names Catch a Bid Amid Macro Uncertainty
briefs.body: Worthington Steel climbed 5.91% Wednesday, contributing to Materials' sector-leading 1.17% advance. The move fits a broader pattern of investors rotating toward hard-asset names when geopolitical and macro crosscurrents cloud the outlook. Analysts note that elevated overseas bond yields may be amplifying the relative appeal of commodity-exposed equities.

briefs.headline: Somnigroup Pops as Consumer-Durables Buying Picks Up
briefs.body: Somnigroup International rose 6.55%, making it one of the session's top three gainers and a bright spot within the Consumer sector, which finished up 0.87%. The move suggests selective appetite for domestically oriented consumer names even as rate pressures persist globally. Skyworks Solutions also added 6.32%, rounding out a strong day for non-software technology-adjacent stocks.
